input: In this cost review, we take a detailed look at the transportation costs associated with the returns flow, drawing on the carrier invoices from the last 12 months in order to build a comprehensive picture of what this flow is costing the business on an annual basis. The returns flow involves a substantial amount of vehicle movement: each individual trip covers a distance of 737 km, and the carrier charges a rate of $1.6 per km, which means that the derived cost of a single trip works out to $1179.2. Over the course of a full year, the business undertakes a total of 857 trips of this kind, covering a derived total distance of 631609 km, and when all of these elements are brought together, the annual transport cost comes to $1011k. It is important to note that the trip count on which this figure rests includes empty running, so the annual total does not relate solely to vehicles carrying returned goods; vehicles travelling empty are also captured within the 857 trips and are charged at the same $1.6 per km. Overall, the figure of $1011k therefore represents the full invoiced cost of operating the returns flow over the last 12 months, reflecting the combined effect of the distance per trip, the rate per kilometre, and the number of trips undertaken.
target: Returns transport costs $1011k a year. The figure comes from the carrier invoices for the last 12 months and covers the returns flow in full: 857 trips a year at 737 km per trip and $1.6 per km. Distance accounts for most of the total. The 857 trips cover a derived 631609 km a year, and each trip carries a derived cost of $1179.2. Three quantities set the total, and each stands on the invoice base: the trip count, the distance per trip, and the rate. A change in the annual figure has to enter through one of the three. The per-trip cost is the unit figure in the review: any comparison between carriers, or between the returns flow and an alternative arrangement, is made on that figure and on the trip count it multiplies. The trip count includes empty running. Empty kilometres are therefore paid for at the same $1.6 per km as loaded kilometres, and the $1011k is the cost of the returns flow as operated, not the cost of moving returned goods alone. No split of the total into a loaded part and an empty part can be read from the trip count. The evidence base is one year of carrier invoices. The review states the level of the cost over the last 12 months at the invoiced distance and rate. With no earlier period in the base, the review shows what the returns flow costs and not whether that cost is rising or falling.
